n: Better a dry crust eaten in peace than a house full of feasting with conflict. Sacrificial meat was often eaten at feasts, so this means a house full of party food.

f.g: A crust of bread with no oil or dip.
Feasts—meat from peace offerings was eaten at celebrations.

n: A wise servant can rise above a shameful son and even share the family inheritance. Character can count for more than birth.

f.w: A wise servant shall have rule

n: Silver and gold are refined by intense heat, but the Lord tests hearts. Trials can purify us.

f.g: fining pot = a crucible for refining metal.

n: Wrongdoers eagerly listen to wicked talk, and liars give ear to destructive words. People seek out what matches their character.

f.g: A destructive, wicked tongue.

n: Mocking the poor insults their Creator; delighting in someone else’s disaster won’t go unpunished.
Grandchildren are the crown of the elderly, and parents are the pride of their children. Families bless each other across generations.

f.w: Children's children are the crown of old men

n: Fine speech doesn’t suit a fool, and lying suits a leader even less.

f.g: becometh = suits, is fitting for.

n: To the one who gives it, a bribe seems like a magic stone that opens every door. This describes how people view bribes; other verses condemn them.

f.g: Here, a bribe.

n: Overlooking an offense builds love; repeating it spreads division and breaks up close friends.

f.w: He that covereth a transgression seeketh love

f.g: Close friends.

n: One rebuke goes deeper into a wise person than a hundred lashes into a fool.

f.g: stripes = lashes, blows.

n: A rebel seeks only trouble, so a stern messenger will be sent against him.

f.g: A merciless messenger—perhaps an executioner or messenger of judgment.

n: Humorous and vivid: you’d be safer meeting an enraged mother bear than a fool caught up in his folly.

f.w: a bear robbed of her whelps
f.g: whelps = cubs.

n: Whoever repays good with evil will find evil never leaves his household—as David learned after his sin against Uriah.
Starting a quarrel is like opening a floodgate—once the water flows, it’s hard to stop. Drop the matter before it breaks out.

f.g: Like a small crack in a dam that quickly becomes a flood.

n: Acquitting the guilty and condemning the innocent are both detestable to God. Justice must be fair both ways.
What good is money in a fool’s hand to buy wisdom when he has no desire for it? Wisdom can’t be bought without a willing heart.

f.w: he hath no heart to it
f.g: He has no sense or desire to learn.

n: A true friend loves through every season, and family members are born to help in hard times.

f.w: A friend loveth at all times

f.g: adversity = hardship, distress.

n: Only a person lacking sense shakes hands to co-sign a neighbor’s debt.

f.g: Shakes hands to seal a pledge.

n: Loving conflict means loving sin. Building a high gate—showing off—invites disaster.

f.g: Builds a lofty doorway—a show of pride; or “opens his mouth wide” in boasting.

n: A crooked heart finds no good, and a deceitful tongue lands in trouble.

f.g: froward = crooked, perverse.

n: Raising a fool brings grief; the father of a godless fool has no joy.

f.g: Here Hebrew naval—a morally empty, godless person.

n: A cheerful heart is good medicine; a crushed spirit dries a person up. Joy has real effects on health.

f.w: A merry heart doeth good like a medicine

n: A wicked person secretly accepts a bribe from under the cloak to twist justice.

f.g: From a fold in the garment—slipped secretly.

n: The discerning keep wisdom in view; a fool’s eyes wander to the ends of the earth, never focused.

f.w: the eyes of a fool are in the ends of the earth
f.g: His attention drifts everywhere except what matters.

n: A foolish child brings grief to a father and bitterness to a mother.

f.g: His mother—she who bore him.

n: It is wrong to punish the innocent or to strike noble people for doing what is right.

f.g: equity = uprightness, fairness.

n: A person of knowledge uses words with restraint and keeps a calm, cool spirit.

f.g: Literally “cool of spirit”—calm, even-tempered.

n: Even a fool seems wise if he keeps quiet. Silence is sometimes the wisest speech.
